Update: The broken clustering issue is the same as the one documented for the 4.3.0 release in this ticket:

The branch seems to be OK. Using "mvn jetty:run" on Windows, I tested forwards/backwards compatibility by creating/retrieving a few object and datastreams through the UI. I haven't tried any ISPN configurations yet.
, have you had a chance to verify backward/forward compatibility of this ticket?
Not yet, but I will soon.
in terms of backwards compatibility, I did not encounter any errors.

I checked out this branch, merged in all updates from master, built it and installed it on top of an existing repository that uses the default configuration (leveldb for properties and a directory for binaries). Everything appeared to work as expected: I could calculate fixity on previously added binary resources; I could create, retrieve, update and delete resources. I also ran the fcrepo-camel and fcrepo-camel-toolbox integration tests against that version.
, feel free to merge and close this PR if you are happy with it.

This task is to upgrade F4's Modeshape dependency to 4.3.0.Final

Modeshape 4.3.0.Final jumps Infinispan versions to 7.2.0.Final, more than a major version number jump. None of the Infinispan configurations now in the code base will even parse with the new version, let alone run. They must all be rewritten, and in the case of clustering config, from scratch.

However, there is a bug in ISPN that will be addressed in:

  • ISPN 7.2.3, and
  • Mode 4.4.0
    See: https://issues.jboss.org/browse/MODE-2471

Testing should focus on forwards/backwards compatibility with populated F4 repos.
The fact that clustering is broken with these configurations will be addressed separately.
Update: The broken clustering issue is the same as the one documented for the 4.3.0 release in this ticket: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1739

The branch seems to be OK. Using "mvn jetty:run" on Windows, I tested forwards/backwards compatibility by creating/retrieving a few object and datastreams through the UI. I haven't tried any ISPN configurations yet.
Unknown, have you had a chance to verify backward/forward compatibility of this ticket?

Andrew Woods in terms of backwards compatibility, I did not encounter any errors.

I checked out this branch, merged in all updates from master, built it and installed it on top of an existing repository that uses the default configuration (leveldb for properties and a directory for binaries). Everything appeared to work as expected: I could calculate fixity on previously added binary resources; I could create, retrieve, update and delete resources. I also ran the fcrepo-camel and fcrepo-camel-toolbox integration tests against that version.

Thanks, Unknown and Osman Din.
Unknown, feel free to merge and close this PR if you are happy with it.
